summary:
IWG, the flexible workspace operator behind Regus and Spaces, signed 728 new locations in the first half of 2026, a 47% increase over the 496 signed in H1 2025. It opened 425 locations versus 338 a year earlier. Interim results released August 11 showed revenue of $2.4 billion, up 11% from $2.2 billion.

Growth is driven by IWG's capital-light managed partnership model, which accounted for roughly 95% of H1 signings. Revenue from managed and franchised locations rose 36% year over year, and recurring management fees climbed 84% to $35 million. Company-owned locations generated $1.865 billion, up 5% from $1.77 billion.

The U.S. led new signings with 187, followed by the U.K. with 62, India with 45 and China with 42. Asia Pacific contributed 164 signings, more than a fifth of the global total. IWG is deliberately targeting locations beyond major business centers, including suburbs, commuter towns and regional cities. The company estimates roughly 1.2 billion white-collar workers globally represent a market opportunity worth more than $2 trillion.

In July, IWG acquired French operator Wojo from Bouygues Immobilier and Accor, adding 186 locations and creating a longer-term relationship with Accor that could enable flexible workspace inside additional hotels.

At the end of H1, IWG had 358,000 rooms open globally with a further 257,000 signed and awaiting opening. Once those are open and mature, IWG expects them to produce more than $2 billion in annual system-wide revenue. The portfolio now exceeds 6,000 locations worldwide, underscoring the strategy of extending flexible workspace well beyond traditional central business districts.
